_README.what: The 34 Luck Traits from Sieg's Guide, in the Doc's own three categories. Authority is oks/pathfinder/house-rules/luck.md; the rule text is the Luck Google Doc.
_README.the_purchase_rule: '25 Permanent E-Kats can be used to purchase a Luck Trait.' And, decisively: 'Luck Traits may only be purchased with E-Kats. These Traits do not grant 1 extra luck.' They are NOT character traits -- data/traits.csv must never contain them and trait_selector must never draw them. An earlier pass put Expanded Luck and Big Savings in that CSV; both were removed.
_README.no_double_count: 'These Traits do not grant 1 extra luck' is the mirror of the E-Kat feats' rule. No trait here contributes the generic +1 Luck. Only 'Increase Luck' moves the score at all, by its own stated +1 per stack; validate_luck.py asserts no other trait carries luck_score_bonus.
_README.repeatable: The Doc marks ten traits 'Repeatable' and the three Loot Boxes 'Does not stack'. The remainder are unmarked, and are recorded here as repeatable:false -- the conservative reading, and the one the variety-first picker wants anyway. If the Doc is later clarified, this field is the single place to change.
_README.categories: standard (19) | negative (10) | dimorphic (5). Category is an ELIGIBILITY GATE: dimorphic traits require the Dimorphic luck type; negative traits require a negative luck score.
_README.negative_traits_are_unreachable: No generated character can buy the ten negative-luck traits, and this is a consequence of three separate rulings rather than an oversight: negative luck comes only from selling; sellers take no E-Kat feats (or the feats' luck bonus would hand the sold luck straight back, making selling free money); no E-Kat feats means no starting reserve; no reserve means no purchase. They are curated anyway so the roster is complete, a player can hand-add one with real data behind it, and check_luck can ASSERT the unreachability rather than assume it.
_README.pf1_change_candidate: Marks traits whose effect is a real pf1 modifier (DR, natural AC, save bonuses) rather than an in-play action. None is wired into feat_changes.json: every one of them sits in the unreachable negative set, so nothing would ever emit them. Wire them at the same time as whatever makes those traits reachable.

effect_fields.luck_cap_step: raises the positive luck cap, per stack
effect_fields.luck_score_bonus: raises the luck score itself, per stack
effect_fields.e_kat_store_step: raises the 99 E-Kat storage cap, per stack
effect_fields.twist_fate_bonus: extra Twist of Fate uses per day, per stack
effect_fields.vault_cap_step: raises the Vaulted Interest limit cap, per stack

_README.prerequisites: Luck Traits have prerequisites in three forms and all three are enforced by luck_trait_chooser: (a) another TRAIT -- the Loot Box chain and Never-Ending Suffering; (b) requires_luck_at_most, a FLOOR on how negative the score must be, which every negative trait carries; (c) requires_luck_assets_per_stack, Inevitable's count of luck feats+traits, which scales per stack. The Doc's trait section bleeds into the feat list -- Very Lucky Boy, It Just Works and Luck God appear there with prerequisites but are FEATS, and live in e_kat_feats.json.

Expanded Luck.benefit: Your luck cap is increased by +5.

Lucky Survivor.benefit: Each Luck Point can reduce damage by 2 rather than one.

Increase Luck.benefit: Gain a +1 to your luck score.

E-Kat Exchange: Momentum.benefit: +1 E-Kat everytime you are on the receiving end of a crit or crit failure that results in a benefit for you.

Lucky Survival.benefit: Add your luck score to your AC/Saves against a single attack once per day.

God Has Failed Us.benefit: Gain 2 E-Kats in any session the GM does not place an E-Kat onscreen.

E-Kat Exchange: Loaded Dice.benefit: Choose the result of one percentile for 40 E-Kats.

E-Kat Exchange: Pull.benefit: Reroll a percentile, choose between the 2 results for 10 E-Kats.

E-Kat Exchange: Aim-Bot.benefit: After a roll which did not crit, reroll twice and if any dice crit use those instead for 10 E-Kats.

E-Kat Exchange: Auto-Dodge.benefit: After an enemy crit, they reroll twice and if neither attacks crit, avoid the attack altogether 10 E-Kats.

E-Kat Exchange: Loot Box.benefit: Increase loot table roll by one category before the roll for 25 E-Kats.

E-Kat Exchange: Premium Loot Box.benefit: Increase loot table roll by two categories before the roll for 50 E-Kats.

E-Kat Exchange: Deluxe Loot Box.benefit: Increase loot table roll by three categories before the roll for 75 E-Kats.

E-Kat Exchange: Optimal Allocation.benefit: Choose the allocation for 1 earned inherent roll for 10 E-Kats.

E-Kat Exchange: Convenient Failure.benefit: Instant fail a skill check, save, or attack of your choice for a cost of 1 E-Kat.

E-Kat Exchange: Lucky Navigator.benefit: Succeed on a navigation check for 5 E-Kats.

E-Kat Exchange: Blind Luck.benefit: Ignore Miss Chance that would have negated a successful attack for 5 E-Kats.

E-Kat Exchange: Rotten Luck.benefit: Ignore targets luck and any luck bonuses for one roll for a number of E-kats according to the following formula.
E-Kat Exchange: Rotten Luck.note: The Doc says 'according to the following formula' and the formula did not come through the extraction. Re-read before anything depends on the cost.

When It Counts.benefit: Once per day you may use your negative luck as a luck pool as if you had the feat 'lucky survivor', mitigating the damage to a minimum of one.

Trauma Survivor.benefit: Add your negative luck score to the hitpoint threshold at which you die.

Never-Ending Suffering.benefit: When unconscious with Trauma Survivor active, enemies take a penalty equal to your luck score to notice you.
Never-Ending Suffering.no_change_reason: Penalises an ENEMY's Perception check to notice you, so there is nothing on this character's own sheet to attach it to. A note on skill.per would surface in the wrong actor's tooltip. The benefit text renders on the trait item; the GM applies it.

Tough Luck.benefit: Gain DR/- equal to your luck mod.

context_notes.text: Damage reduction equal to the magnitude of your luck modifier, overcome by nothing (DR n/-).

Tough Skin.benefit: Gain Natural AC equal to your luck mod.

Seen it all.benefit: Add your luck Mod to any Fear, Morale, or Illusion based Saves.

context_notes.text: Add the magnitude of your luck modifier to saving throws against Fear, Morale or Illusion effects.

Hardened Mind.benefit: Add your luck mod to Will Saves

Hardened Body.benefit: Add your luck mod to Fort Saves

Hardened Reflexes.benefit: Add your luck mod to Ref Saves

Been there done that.benefit: Crit Penalty Luck Rolls are one category higher.

Fated Survival.benefit: Upon failing a Twist of Fate you may reroll and try again once a day.

Extra Spin.benefit: You gain an additional Twist of Fate per day.

Interest Growth.benefit: Upon rolling below 0 on a percentile you gain an additional 1 interest.

Big Savings.benefit: Increase Vaulted Interest Limit Cap by 77.

Inevitable.benefit: Auto wins a single Twist of Fate per day.
Inevitable.note: "10 Luck Feats/Traits/E-kat Feats are required for each time you take this feat" -- the requirement scales with the stack, so a second Inevitable needs 20.
